title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography technology was deployed with no human review to verify consent or authenticity. A platform with 13 million monthly visitors hosted sexually explicit videos with the faces of Dutch celebrities, politicians, athletes and members of the royal family digitally placed onto pornographic footage. The system monetized uploads by paying users based on video views, creating financial incentive to produce nonconsensual sexual imagery at scale.

The failure was one of governance, not detection. The platform operated with minimal friction for creating and distributing illegal content, leaving enforcement entirely to victims filing complaints after harm occurred. A legal expert noted that without government intervention, more such videos would appear. Whether the platform's design was deliberately indifferent to illegal use, or negligent in failing to anticipate it, is not established.

summary:
Several female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos posted on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature the faces of Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. The interim Justice Minister called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to news outlets that they have filed reports or are considering legal action.

The deepfake pornography involves digitally placing a celebrity's head onto footage of pornographic actors. Users who upload material receive payment based on video views, and the platform advises them to remain anonymous. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake pornography featuring celebrities will appear. Deepfake material falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Victims can file complaints with prosecutors who may attempt to shut down the website, or pursue other options including class action lawsuits and complaints to data protection authorities. A similar case previously resulted in a conditional sentence for a 39-year-old man.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
